source.title: Reason to Rote: Rethinking Memorization in Reasoning
source.authors: Yu-Pei Du; Philipp Mondorf; Silvia Casola; Yue-Kun Yao; Robert Litschko; Barbara Plank

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether noisy-label memorization can coexist with clean-example generalization in a new setting: small Transformer language models trained from scratch on synthetic arithmetic and relational reasoning tasks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own learning-dynamics, probing, and intervention results. It cites prior noisy-label studies, but those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: R1–R2 test the coexistence component of V1 in a new setting: Transformers fit a small, fixed subset of corrupted training labels while achieving high clean held-out accuracy. They do not test fitting an entirely random-labeled dataset or chance-level held-out performance under random labels.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that, on these controlled tasks, noisy-label memorization retains and relies on reasoning computations, uses distributed encodings, and in FDA involves outlier shifts in higher-layer MLP neuron activations.
record.recipe_differences: Small decoder-only Transformers trained from scratch on synthetic arithmetic and relational tasks with a small fraction of corrupted training labels; the study also uses probes and causal activation interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Task and model size affect performance: the paper reports that two-hop reasoning requires larger models, and wider FDA models memorize better. The authors also report that noise rate affects generalization and omit some weak-model/noise-rate combinations.

fits_no_version.finding: Correct-label information remains decodable in intermediate representations after noisy-label memorization, including in reinitialized Qwen2.5-0.5B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Models can retain intermediate correct-answer computations while outputting memorized corrupted labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing bridge-entity information impairs memorization; patching pre-memorization MLP activations preferentially disrupts memorized outputs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy-label memorization can reuse reasoning computations and depend on changes in higher-layer MLP activations.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The study uses synthetic tasks and relatively small models trained from scratch. Several intervention findings are described qualitatively from figures, with no numerical uncertainty reported in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying outcome rows were identified beyond the learning-dynamics, probe, intervention, and larger-model results recorded above.

untested.parts: Entirely random-labeled training sets; held-out accuracy against random labels; matched separate natural-label and random-label training runs; the named image architectures and datasets; coexistence without explicit regularization. The experiments use synthetic tasks, partial corruption, and AdamW.
Test error as width increases beyond an established zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparisons under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected examples.

missing.what: Model-size and noise-rate comparisons relevant to the scope of coexistence: the FDA 8-layer, 128-hidden model does not memorize all noisy instances; THR with 4 layers and 256 hidden dimensions reaches 68% validation accuracy at 10% noise. Record paired memorization and validation outcomes by configuration where readable. The supplied figure text does not establish whether incomplete FDA memorization remains nearly perfect.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the extracted intervention-based limits_scope verdict. V1 makes no claim of robustness to internal ablations. Model-size comparisons do not test V2 because they do not establish a width threshold for zero training error and examine test error beyond it.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test the named image-model architectures, natural image labels, or random-label held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: FDA model
rows.size_stated: 4 layers, 256 hidden size, and 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Trained on four-digit addition with 5% noisy training labels; tracked accuracy on clean training, noisy training, corrected noisy labels, and clean validation examples.
rows.measure: Accuracy on Train-Clean, Mem-Noisy, and Validation; Mem-Corrected accuracy over training steps.
rows.value: By the end of training, all models achieve near-perfect accuracy on Train-Clean, Mem-Noisy, and Validation; Mem-Corrected accuracy reaches ∼100% by step 4,000, then starts to drop after step 5,000 as Mem-Noisy accuracy increases.
rows.note: The clean validation examples use correct addition labels; the noisy training examples have corrupted sums.
rows.check: Scope the result to 5% corrupted training labels and first-answer-token accuracy (the thousands digit), rather than accuracy on complete addition answers.

rows.subject: THR model
rows.size_stated: 8 layers, 256 hidden size, and 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Trained on two-hop relational reasoning with noisy training answers; tracked accuracy on clean and noisy splits.
rows.measure: Accuracy on Train-Clean, Mem-Noisy, Mem-Corrected, and Validation.
rows.value: By the end of training, all models achieve near-perfect accuracy on Train-Clean, Mem-Noisy, and Validation. The model learns the generalizable reasoning output first on noisy instances, although performance never reaches 100%, and eventually memorizes the noisy labels.
rows.note: The paper says Mem-Corrected performance closely matches Validation during the generalization stage.
rows.check: Measures coexistence under partial label corruption, not fitting an entirely random-labeled dataset. The answer entity is a single token.

source_check.locator_found: §2.2–2.3; §3.1; Appendix A; Appendix C; Appendix I, Figure 13.

rows.subject: FDA model
rows.size_stated: 4 layers, 256 hidden size, and 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Applied logit lens to residual streams to predict answer tokens on noisy training instances, their corrected clean labels, and validation examples.
rows.measure: Answer-token accuracy on Mem-Corrected and Mem-Noisy.
rows.note: The result indicates that correct-label information remains detectable on noisy training instances after memorization.
rows.check: Intermediate-layer decoding measures retained correct-label information, not held-out generalization or random-label fitting capacity. The approximately 10% Mem-Noisy value is a comparison target, not a control baseline.

rows.subject: THR model
rows.size_stated: 8 layers, 256 hidden size, and 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Used a linear probe on residual streams to predict answer tokens on noisy training instances and their corrected clean labels.
rows.note: The paper reports this as evidence that clean-label computations persist in hidden layers.
rows.check: Probe accuracy on corrected noisy training examples measures decodable information, not the generalization behavior named in V1.

rows.subject: THR model
rows.size_stated: 8 layers, 256 hidden size, and 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Removed linearly detectable bridge-entity signals from residual streams using INLP and patched the modified streams back into the model.
rows.measure: Average prediction probability for the answer token on Mem-Noisy and Validation.
rows.value: Removing bridge entities substantially harms memorization, especially at layer 2; the impact is milder than on clean-label computation for Validation.
rows.note: Intervention result on dependence between generalization computations and memorization.
rows.check: Bridge-entity ablation measures causal dependence of memorization on intermediate computations. Its effect does not qualify or contradict V1's coexistence claim.

rows.subject: FDA model
rows.size_stated: 4 layers, 256 hidden size, and 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: Replaced post-memorization MLP activations with pre-memorization activations and measured faithfulness on noisy training and validation examples.
rows.value: Patching pre-memorization activations sharply reduces memorization faithfulness, while only slightly affecting validation faithfulness; validation accuracy is restored to 100%.
rows.note: Shows a tradeoff under an internal intervention; it does not negate the reported coexistence of clean generalization and noisy-label memorization.
rows.check: Activation-patching faithfulness measures an internal mechanism under intervention. V1 does not claim coexistence survives such interventions, so the extracted limits_scope interpretation is unwarranted.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-0.5B
rows.operation_detail: Trained on FDA with 5% noisy labels and examined logit-lens predictions across layers.
rows.measure: Answer-token accuracy for Mem-Corrected and Mem-Noisy across layers.
rows.value: The model first computes the correct label for noisy training instances in early layers, then overwrites these predictions with memorized corrupted labels in later layers.
rows.note: The authors describe this as establishing coexistence of both mechanisms after memorization.
rows.check: Layerwise decoding on noisy training instances does not establish clean held-out accuracy for Qwen. This row alone cannot demonstrate V1's behavioral coexistence.

relationships.condition: Selected FDA and THR Transformers trained from scratch with 5% corrupted training labels; first-answer-token evaluation

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: FDA and THR synthetic reasoning tasks; tested trained-from-scratch models
reader_labels.reason: Models eventually memorize noisy training answers while achieving near-perfect clean validation accuracy; clean-label computations also remain detectable on noisy instances (R1–R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: THR bridge-entity ablation and FDA pre-memorization activation patching
reader_labels.reason: Interventions on reasoning-related signals or activations impair memorization to varying degrees, so the coexistence result depends on intact internal computations (R5–R6).
